articles.title: Quem eram pesquisadoras homenageadas em defesa póstuma na Unicamp | G1
articles.standfirst: Doutoranda e orientadora morreram antes da banca de doutorado. Ligadas pela dança, pela pesquisa e pela formação de artistas, deixaram legado acadêmico e artístico reconhecido dentro e fora do país.
articles.summary: Doutoranda e orientadora morreram antes da banca de doutorado. Ligadas pela dança, pela pesquisa e pela formação de artistas, deixaram legado acadêmico e artístico.
articles.body:
A defesa póstuma inédita realizada pela Unicamp na segunda-feira (24) transformou uma tese em homenagem ao encontro de duas pesquisadoras que se cruzaram pela dança e pela universidade. A tese "Compostagem como prática performativa: processos imersivos em dança e permacultura" foi desenvolvida por Carla Vendramin e Silvia Geraldi, que morreram antes da banca.

Vendramin morreu em janeiro de 2024, em Porto Alegre (RS), aos 51 anos, em decorrência de um incêndio. Já Geraldi faleceu em julho de 2025, em Campinas (SP), aos 61 anos, por conta de uma doença congênita.

As duas pesquisadoras integravam o grupo "Prática como Pesquisa", no qual o corpo e a experiência artística eram considerados centrais para a produção de conhecimento.

Carla Vendramin (à esquerda) e Silvia Geraldi (à direita): responsáveis pela pesquisa — Foto: Redes sociais

Para a professora Marisa Martins Lambert, que assumiu a condução da defesa após a morte de Silvia, as duas compartilhavam uma preocupação comum: pensar respostas para questões sociais, ambientais e políticas por meio da arte.

"São pessoas que estão pensando futuros para os nossos contextos políticos, ambientais e sociais", afirmou a professora em entrevista ao g1 . "O trabalho traz a ideia da compostagem, dessa reciclagem contínua. E nós voltamos para a terra e a terra gera as novas sementes", refletiu Lambert.

Artista, pesquisadora e professora Carla Vendramin — Foto: Redes sociais

Natural de Caxias do Sul (RS), Carla Vendramin era artista, pesquisadora e professora vinculada ao curso de Licenciatura em Dança da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS). Também possuía mestrado em Coreografia pela Middlesex University, em Londres.

Ao longo da carreira, desenvolveu trabalhos voltados à dança, educação, acessibilidade e práticas corporais. Entre 2005 e 2010, participou de projetos educacionais da companhia britânica Candoco Dance Company, reconhecida internacionalmente por integrar artistas com e sem deficiência.

Também colaborou com iniciativas em Portugal, Inglaterra e Itália voltadas à inclusão por meio da dança. Na UFRGS, coordenou o projeto de extensão "Diversos Corpos Dançantes" e se dedicou ao estudo de práticas de dança para grupos com diferentes habilidades.

Nos últimos anos, concentrou sua pesquisa na relação entre dança, permacultura, agrofloresta e meio ambiente. Sua tese investigou como práticas ecológicas podem dialogar com processos artísticos e educacionais contemporâneos.

Para Lambert, Carla "conseguiu abrir novas portas de saber sem uma preocupação do que isso resultaria para ela, mas pela própria pesquisa em si", mobilizando temas considerados fundamentais para os desafios atuais.

Segundo a professora, uma das principais contribuições de Carla Vendramin foi propor uma visão em que corpo e natureza não aparecem como elementos separados. "Nós somos o ambiente, nós somos parte, nós somos terra", resumiu.

Artista, educadora e pesquisadora Silvia Geraldi — Foto: Reprodução/Unicamp

Professora do Instituto de Artes da Unicamp , Silvia Maria Geraldi foi considerada por colegas uma das figuras mais importantes da dança contemporânea brasileira. Artista, educadora e pesquisadora, morreu aos 61 anos, em julho de 2025.

Sua formação acadêmica foi construída integralmente na Unicamp. Graduou-se em Ciência da Computação, fez mestrado em Educação, doutorado em Artes e pós-doutorado em Artes da Cena. Posteriormente tornou-se livre-docente do Departamento de Artes Corporais.

Silvia atuava na graduação em Dança e no Programa de Pós-Graduação em Artes da Cena. Entre 2017 e 2021, coordenou o programa e participou do processo que levou o curso ao conceito 6 da Capes, nível considerado de excelência acadêmica.

Pesquisava temas ligados à corporeidade, estudos somáticos, dramaturgia, improvisação, processos de criação e feminismos na dança. Também liderava o grupo de pesquisa "Prática como Pesquisa", dedicado à produção de conhecimento a partir da experiência artística e corporal.

Além da carreira acadêmica, dançou em grupos importantes da cena contemporânea brasileira, integrou a Companhia de Danças de Diadema e fundou, em 2000, a Silvia Geraldi Cia de Dança, voltada à criação em dança contemporânea.

Foi Silvia quem iniciou o processo para que a tese de Carla pudesse chegar à banca mesmo após a morte da aluna. Segundo Marisa Lambert, a orientadora considerava fundamental que o trabalho fosse disponibilizado à comunidade acadêmica e publicado para alcançar outros pesquisadores.

"Ela imediatamente desejou que esse trabalho pudesse ser colocado no repositório da Unicamp e eventualmente publicado e disseminado", afirmou Lambert.

articles.title: Vida de luxo nas redes e rastro de calotes: as dívidas na Justiça da empresária Roberta Luchsinger | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigada pela PF responde a ações judiciais por calotes que vão de aluguéis em área nobre e mensalidades escolares a serviços prestados por trabalhadores autônomos.
articles.summary: Investigada pela PF responde a ações judiciais por calotes que vão de aluguéis em área nobre e mensalidades escolares a serviços prestados por trabalhadores autônomos.
articles.body:
Nas redes sociais, ela se apresenta como uma empresária de sucesso, compartilhando viagens internacionais, jantares em restaurantes caros e rotina de alto padrão. Nas páginas da Justiça, no entanto, a realidade é oposta: Roberta Luchsinger acumula derrotas em processos de dívidas não pagas que atingem diferentes perfis de credores em São Paulo e Minas Gerais.

A apuração sobre os processos revela um padrão nas ações judiciais. Em diversas ocasiões, oficiais de justiça não conseguiram localizar a empresária nos endereços informados para intimá-la. Também não foram encontrados bens ou valores em contas bancárias para penhora.

Em duas ações, Roberta alegou que não tem capacidade financeira para arcar com os custos do processo.

A empresária figura em investigações da Polícia Federal sobre suspeitas de corrupção e tráfico de influência em Brasília.

O inquérito apura ligações de Roberta com Marco Aurélio Ribeiro, o Marcola, ex-chefe de gabinete da Presidência; Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, o Lulinha, filho mais velho do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva; e o lobista Antônio Carlos Antunes, conhecido como "Careca do INSS", apontado como operador de fraudes em benefícios previdenciários e preso preventivamente.

"Não fiz pagamentos ao Marcola. Eu ajudei um amigo. Óbvio, eu deveria ter sido atenta ao fato de ser ele chefe de gabinete do presidente. Mas é covardia 'linkar' uma coisa na outra", afirmou na ocasião.

Roberta Luchsinger é investigada pela PF — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Sobre a relação com Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, o Lulinha, Roberta disse: "Eu e Fábio somos amigos. Já tivemos intenção de fazermos coisas juntos fora do âmbito público, porém, sabemos que qualquer coisa que ele faça sempre será mal vista."

O trânsito no meio político teve início a partir de 2011, época de seu casamento com o ex-deputado federal Protógenes Queiroz (PCdoB), de quem se separou em 2014.

Em 2017, a empresária passou a se apresentar publicamente como herdeira de um fundador do banco suíço Credit Suisse. Registros civis, porém, apontam que seu avô, Pedro Paulo Arnaldo Luchsinger, nasceu no Rio de Janeiro em 1927 e era proprietário de uma lavanderia. Questionada, informou não possuir documentos que comprovem a origem suíça do familiar.

Em 2016, a empresária e uma sócia de uma produtora apresentaram ao investidor Lauro um projeto de documentário sobre o designer de carros de luxo Horacio Pagani.

A orçamentação previra gastos de 4 milhões de dólares, valor que seria coberto por um fundo de investimento do Bahrein.

Para iniciar as gravações antes da liberação do montante internacional, foi necessário um empréstimo ponte de 300 mil dólares (cerca de R$ 1,5 milhão na cotação da época).

Roberta convenceu Lauro a figurar como avalista da operação, oferecendo como garantia uma fazenda de sua propriedade em Minas Gerais em troca de participação na bilheteria e comissão de R$ 40 mil.

O aporte estrangeiro não se concretizou, as parcelas do empréstimo não foram quitadas e o credor obteve na Justiça a posse da fazenda do avalista, avaliada em R$ 8 milhões.

"O projeto do filme era bonito, uma história que valia a pena vender para investidores. Acabei aceitando a proposta. Tudo o que eu tinha estava lá. Não é a questão da propriedade em si, é o sonho", desabafou Lauro.

Processo envolvendo Roberta Luchsinger — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A lista de credores inclui profissionais autônomos e estabelecimentos de serviços. Em 2011, a empresária contratou os serviços do tapeceiro Nilton Cezar para reformar estofados, camas e revestimentos de sua residência pelo valor de R$ 61 mil.

Após o pagamento inicial de R$ 25 mil, o saldo restante não foi quitado. O profissional acionou o Judiciário e obteve ganho de causa em todas as instâncias, incluindo o Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ). Acordos celebrados ao longo da execução judicial foram descumpridos.

"A gente tem um baque porque precisa pagar funcionário e aluguel do ponto. Chegamos a vender um carro por causa disso", relatou o tapeceiro.

Para estancar o processo, a empresária ofereceu à Justiça uma coleção de 14 gravuras avaliadas por ela em R$ 70 mil, apresentadas como obras originais de Cândido Portinari. Diante da entrega, o processo foi suspenso.

No entanto, o Projeto Portinari, entidade responsável pela autenticação do acervo do artista, confirmou que as peças eram reproduções impressas sem valor de originalidade.

Outras ações judiciais somam débitos com:

Instituição de ensino : Dívida de R$ 91 mil referente a mensalidades escolares não pagas da filha ao longo de 2017.

Comércio de vestuário : Compra de R$ 6.124 realizada em 2017 em loja de roupas, cujo valor atualizado pela Justiça ultrapassa R$ 21 mil. Um quadro oferecido pela ré como garantia de R$ 100 mil desapareceu antes do leilão judicial.

Marketing político : Contratação de agência de publicidade em 2022 por R$ 42 mil para pré-campanha eleitoral, com quitação de apenas R$ 4.200.

Direitos trabalhistas : Processos movidos por uma babá e uma empregada doméstica demitidas sem verbas rescisórias, que somavam R$ 50 mil e prescreveram sem que os valores fossem recebidos.

Em 2019, a empresária passou a residir em um apartamento de alto padrão em São Paulo.

Proprietários do imóvel, um casal de idosos que dependia do aluguel para complementar a renda, moveram ação de despejo em 2020 por inadimplência contínua de aluguel, condomínio e IPTU.

A desocupação do imóvel ocorreu apenas em 2023. O proprietário morreu no decorrer da tramitação judicial sem receber os valores. A dívida acumulada, que chegou a R$ 500 mil, só foi quitada em maio de 2024.

Procurada para se manifestar sobre os processos citados, Roberta Luchsinger optou por não gravar entrevista. Ela enviou uma relação de números de processos informando quais ações já foram arquivadas pelo Judiciário.

A respeito do caso envolvendo a fazenda em Minas Gerais, alegou ter sido igualmente enganada pelo investidor do projeto e sustentou que o proprietário do imóvel tinha ciência dos riscos da operação financeira.

articles.title: Jotapê faz apresentação surpresa na Praia do Leme | G1
articles.standfirst: Empunhando seu violão, o artista tocou a música nova “Até Outro Dia Amor” e alguns sucessos no trecho da praia conhecido como Rasta Beach.
articles.summary: Empunhando seu violão, o artista tocou a música nova “Até Outro Dia Amor” e alguns sucessos no trecho da praia conhecido como Rasta Beach.
articles.body:
O cantor e compositor Jotapê surpreendeu banhistas da Praia do Leme neste domingo (30) com uma apresentação surpresa.

Empunhando seu violão, o artista tocou a música nova “Até Outro Dia Amor” e alguns sucessos como "Ouro Marrom" no trecho da praia conhecido como Rasta Beach.

No local e nas redes sociais os espectadores elogiaram a iniciativa. "O Rio de Janeiro é muito legal", postou um banhista com um vídeo da apresentação". "Hoje ainda teve um show do Jotapê no Rasta, lá no leme. Foi gostosinho", escreveu outro.

articles.title: 'No Brasil acontecem nossos maiores shows', diz Dave Grohl | G1
articles.standfirst: Baterista do Nirvana e fundador do Foo Fighters, músico relembra a carreira, as perdas pessoais e a relação com o público brasileiro em entrevista ao Fantástico.
articles.summary: Baterista do Nirvana e fundador do Foo Fighters, músico relembra a carreira, as perdas pessoais e a relação com o público brasileiro em entrevista ao Fantástico.
articles.body:
A história de Dave Grohl tinha tudo para dar errado. Aos 17 anos, o filho de uma professora do estado da Virgínia, nos Estados Unidos, abandonou a escola, saiu de casa e decidiu viver da música, tocando bateria em uma banda de punk rock chamada Scream.

Quatro anos depois, ele trocou o grupo formado por amigos por uma banda alternativa que mudaria sua vida: o Nirvana.

Como baterista do grupo, Dave Grohl marcou o ritmo de uma revolução do grunge. Entre 1990 e 1994, o Nirvana vendeu mais de 15 milhões de álbuns, e Grohl foi reconhecido como um dos melhores bateristas do mundo.

A trajetória, no entanto, foi marcada por uma grande perda. Em 1994, o vocalista e amigo Kurt Cobain morreu, e Dave chegou a pensar em abandonar a música.

Foi tocando que ele encontrou um caminho para superar o luto.

Dave Grohl conta o que espera do show do Foo Fighters no Rock in Rio — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Em 1995, Grohl fundou o Foo Fighters, banda que completa 31 anos e que, desde então, lançou 12 álbuns e ganhou 15 prêmios Grammy.

Em entrevista ao Fantástico, pouco antes de encarar um estádio cheio de fãs em Cleveland, no estado de Ohio, Dave relembrou o início da carreira.

"Quando eu comecei a tocar, eu nunca pensei que isso se tornaria uma carreira. Aí, o Nirvana explodiu e nossas vidas se transformaram", contou o cantor em entrevista ao Fantástico.

Questionado sobre o que diria ao Dave de 10, 12 ou 15 anos, se pudesse voltar no tempo, ele respondeu:

"Eu provavelmente diria que você nunca vai acreditar no que vai acontecer."

A carreira de Dave também ganhou novos capítulos dentro da própria família.

Em 2026, Violet Grohl, filha mais velha do músico, lançou o primeiro álbum. Dave conta que sabia que ela seria musicista desde os quatro anos.

"Essa é uma boa história. Eu sabia que a Violet seria musicista desde que ela tinha quatro anos", afirmou.

Em seu livro, "O Contador de Histórias: Memórias de Vida e de Música" , Dave escreveu: "Nunca fui de colecionar 'coisas'; eu coleciono momentos..."

A relação com a família também aparece quando ele fala da mãe, que considera sua heroína.

Questionado se existe alguma pergunta que odeia responder, Dave disse que não. Segundo ele, gosta de conversar com as pessoas e considera esse um dos traços que herdou da mãe.

"Ela é a sua heroína?", perguntou Carol Cimenti, repórter do Fantástico.

Em 2022, Dave sofreu duas perdas importantes: a mãe e Taylor Hawkins, então baterista do Foo Fighters e um de seus melhores amigos.

Perguntado se a música o ajudou a superar essas perdas, ele respondeu que sim.

"A maneira como consigo, de certa forma, colocar meus sentimentos para fora e me expressar sempre foi através da música", afirmou.

A música, que esteve presente desde o começo da trajetória de Dave, também continua sendo uma forma de conexão com o público.

Foo Fighters se apresenta no The Town 2023 — Foto: Luiz Gabriel Franco/g1

O Foo Fighters se apresenta no Palco Mundo do Rock in Rio na sexta-feira (4), primeiro dia do evento.

Para Dave, os shows no Brasil estão entre os maiores que a banda faz.

"É insano! No Brasil acontecem nossos maiores shows", afirmou.

A repórter lembrou que o público pode chegar a 100 mil pessoas.

"Essa é uma das coisas lindas da música: ela realmente une as pessoas. E o Brasil, a energia que tem lá... vai ser uma loucura total", disse Dave

articles.title: Gunmen chase bike, kill AAP man in Punjab; police suspect poll rivalry
articles.summary: AAP member Gurpreet Singh shot dead in Mamdot, Ferozepur after assailants chased his bike; friend injured. Police probe election rivalry, raids underway.
articles.body: By: Dinesh SharmaFEROZEPUR: An Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) member, Gurpreet Singh alias Gopi, was shot dead and his friend Harpreet Singh alias Happy was injured by armed assailants in a crowded Mamdot village market in Ferozepur around 8pm on Saturday, police said.The assailants chased the victims’ motorcycle in a car, opened fire and shot at a following car carrying nagar panchayat president Rajesh Kumar Maini, who narrowly escaped, according to police.Gurpreet’s friends following in the car rushed both victims to the hospital, where Gurpreet was declared brought dead, while Harpreet was transferred to Ludhiana in stable condition.Gurpreet, who lost his wife one-and-a-half years ago, is survived by two children. Though holding no official AAP title, he was active in nagar panchayat elections and his sister-in-law serves as ward no. 5 councilor.Ferozepur SSP Bhupinder Singh said preliminary findings point to election-related rivalry. He added the accused have been identified and the prime suspect has a criminal history. Police teams are continuously conducting raids to make arrests.The killing sparked criticism of Punjab’s law and order from senior BJP functionary Rana Gurmit Singh Sodhi. Sodhi asserted that the incident reflects the state’s collapsing security, saying leaders who pledged to eliminate crime and drugs at Bhagat Singh’s memorial in Khatkar Kalan have failed. articles.title: Two Malayali women killed in California; friend detained
articles.summary: Two Malayali women, Anjana (35) and Ann Mary Mathew (40), were killed in California; a Malayali friend in the same complex is suspected, police investigating.
articles.body: THRISSUR/THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Two Malayali women were killed in California, United States, allegedly by another Malayali woman who was their friend and lived in the same apartment complex, according to their relatives. An investigation is underway.One of the victims was identified as 35-year-old Anjana from Mudikkode near Mannuthy in Thrissur. The other was Ann Mary Mathew (40) of Kesavadasapuram, Thiruvananthapuram. The victims’ families have alleged that both Anjana and Ann Mary were killed by their friend Anila. According to information received by the families, San Jose police have taken the suspect into custody and are investigating the case.Jerry Sam Joseph, a neighbour and family friend, said Ann Mary’s family had received information that she had an issue with the suspect over a job-related matter. However, Anjana’s cousin Vinod said the family had not yet received any information about the motive behind the killings.The suspect allegedly entered Ann Mary’s house and stabbed her, Jerry said.According to information received by Anjana’s relatives, Anjana was killed after Anila allegedly knocked her down with a car. The killings reportedly took place around noon on Friday (US time). Anjana’s family in Keralam was informed about the incident on Saturday (Indian time).Ann Mary had been living in the US for around 10 years and was working as an engineer, according to her neighbours. She was married to Pallathra Jacob, a native of Chingavanam in Kottayam, who is also in the US.Anjana had been working as a teacher in California for nearly six years, according to her relatives. Her husband, Vijeesh, who hails from Vilangannoor near Peechi, is also employed there. Vijayan Vilangannur, Anjana’s father-in-law, said his son Vijeesh was extremely distressed by the incident and was unable to speak to him.Thrissur collector Sikha Surendran said she had asked Anjana’s family to submit details of the incident so that they could be forwarded to the NORKA secretary, who would then approach Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) for assistance in bringing the body back to the state. articles.title: SEN: Lack of clarity from EA "hurtful and deeply frustrating"
articles.summary: Columba Mailey said "familiarity with the driver is crucial" for his daughter.
articles.body:
A man whose daughter has special educational needs has said it is "hurtful and deeply frustrating" that the Education Authority (EA) still has not clarified what taxi firm will take her to and from school.

Seven-year-old Maisie was using a taxi company provided by the EA but the contract has now gone out to tender.

Her father Columba Mailey said "familiarity with the driver is crucial for Maisie" adding that "24 hours before Maisie starts the new term we have no clarity".

The EA said it understood that changes to transport arrangements can be unsettling and added that it sometimes needs to refresh contracts to ensure value for money.

In February, an agreement for more than £900,000 in savings was reached between the EA and taxi operators.

That came after the EA wrote to taxi drivers asking them to reduce their rates by 10% , or their contract for the work could be terminated.

Mailey, from Greysteel in County Londonderry said: "Maisie is autistic and non-verbal and needs one-to-one supervision at home and at school. That also means in the taxi.

"We were initially told there was no room on a bus for Maisie which led us to the taxi situation in the first place. We were in a good place and she got to know the driver through time and patience."

He told North West Today that Maisie's behavioural needs means she can try to get out of her seat and she is unable to use her voice.

"She needs to build a relationship with any new driver," Mailey added.

"We are now being told a new operator is not appointed yet. We are even being asked by EA Transport if we can get her to school ourselves and they could reimburse us. We are unable to do that due to work commitments. It should not be put back on us."

He added that other parents have come forward to him who find themselves in a similar situation.

"If I didn't make the calls to the EA I would have heard absolutely nothing. Communication has been shocking and it's hurtful as a father and deeply frustrating," he said.

"It's a disgrace and we find as parents we are constantly facing brick walls when it comes to issues around special educational needs."

A spokesperson for the EA said: "We understand that changes to transport arrangements can be unsettling for children with special educational needs, particularly where they rely on routine and familiarity.

"However, the Education Authority has a responsibility to ensure value for money across all services, including home-to-school transport, which means we must periodically refresh contracts."

They added that transport arrangements are based on each child's assessed needs, including any requirement for additional support during the journey.

"Where an adult escort is needed, this is provided to help ensure the child can travel safely and appropriately."

BBC News NI also asked the EA if they could provide details on how many taxi contracts are currently out to tender and how many pupils are in a similar situation in Northern Ireland.

They did not respond to those questions.

articles.title: Grand Canyon flash flood leaves 15 missing, 62 evacuated; further storms feared
articles.summary: US News: An estimated 15 people may be missing and at least 62 have been evacuated after a powerful flash flood tore through parts of Arizona’s Grand Canyon Na.
articles.body: An estimated 15 people may be missing and at least 62 have been evacuated after a powerful flash flood tore through parts of Arizona’s Grand Canyon National Park, destroying footbridges and severely damaging infrastructure, park officials said.The National Park Service said the flooding struck Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Saturday after a series of storms swept through the Grand Canyon. Officials said an earlier working estimate had put the number of missing or unaccounted-for people at 20.No injuries had been reported as of Sunday afternoon, but search and rescue efforts were continuing and more evacuations were planned from Cottonwood Campground and Phantom Ranch.The flooding caused extensive damage across Bright Angel Canyon, with nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek destroyed, cutting off access for hikers. The force of the water also widened the creek bed and created what appeared to be a new rapid, according to the Associated Press.One hiker, David Gregory, told CNN that his group realised something was wrong when the creek near their camp turned black with debris and began flowing rapidly. They were later evacuated by helicopter and taken to safety.The National Park Service has appealed to the public for information about hikers and backpackers who may have been in the affected areas, asking anyone with information to contact its tip line.The threat has not fully passed. Further storms are possible, with rainfall rates of up to 1 inch (2.5 cm) per hour recorded in parts of the canyon. articles.title: Patel to be replaced by Tugendhat as shadow foreign secretary
articles.summary: Kemi Badenoch is expected to carry out a wider reshuffle of her front bench team following high-profile departures.
articles.body:
Former Tory leadership candidate Tom Tugendhat will replace Dame Priti Patel as shadow foreign secretary, BBC News has been told.

As first reported by the Daily Telegraph, he will return to the Conservative front bench when Kemi Badenoch reshuffles her team next month.

Dame Priti wrote on social media that she would be leaving the front bench position to take up a new role focused on strengthening "links with sister parties and centre right movements around the world".

It comes after shadow housing secretary Sir James Cleverly said he was resigning in order to run for London mayor .

The move will see Tugendhat return to a senior role for the first time since finishing fourth in the 2024 Tory leadership election.

The former British Army reserve and Territorial Army officer has long been vocal on international affairs and security matters.

He served as security minister under Liz Truss and Boris Johnson and prior to that spent five years as chair of the Foreign Affairs Select Committee.

Dame Priti was appointed to Badenoch's shadow cabinet after finishing sixth in the leadership election, and previously held senior roles in successive Tory governments, including a three-year spell as home secretary under Boris Johnson.

Announcing her departure in a statement on X, she wrote: "It has been an honour to lead the Party's foreign affairs team in Parliament over the last two years.

"I'm pleased to continue supporting Kemi and the Conservative Party in a new role strengthening our relationships with fellow conservatives and centre right parties around the world."

She said she would continue to serve as the MP for Witham in Essex.

A Conservative reshuffle had already been expected in the coming weeks because of the shadow energy secretary Claire Coutinho's upcoming maternity leave.

In recent weeks, people within the party have played down speculation that the shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride could also lose his job in the changes.

But some sources within the party still believe Badenoch could choose to replace him.

Many within the Conservative Party view Coutinho as a likely future shadow chancellor. The shadow energy secretary is said to have impressed colleagues with her performances in Parliament and the media.

But it is unlikely Badenoch will move to appoint her as shadow chancellor while she is on leave from the front bench.

The Conservative leader will also need to replace Sir James as her shadow housing secretary after he quit the front bench to focus on setting up a campaign to run for London mayor.

He has not yet been selected as the party's candidate for the May 2028 election, nor has he resigned as the MP for Braintree.

articles.title: Gato Leer: gato devolvido por ser 'dependente' é adotado no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Leer foi resgatado com calicivirose e recebeu mais de 100 manifestações de interesse depois que a ONG divulgou a devolução nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: Após ser rejeitado por carinho excessivo, o gato Leer superou a calicivirose e encontrou um novo lar em Porto Alegre através da ONG Gatinhos de Atlântida.
articles.body:
O gato Leer ganhou um novo lar depois que uma publicação sobre a devolução dele mobilizou interessados nas redes sociais. Segundo a ONG "Gatinhos de Atlântida", responsável pelo resgate, a primeira tutora informou que não permaneceria com o animal porque ele seria "dependente demais".

Três dias após da devolução, o projeto publicou a história do gato. De acordo com a ONG, mais de 100 pedidos de adoção foram recebidos após publicações com a foto viralizarem no X (antigo Twitter). Uma nova foto de Leer, dessa vez com uma expressão feliz, viralizou.

O estudante de arquitetura e urbanismo da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) Carlos Eduardo Oliveira foi selecionado para receber Leer em Porto Alegre. O gato havia sido encontrado em uma colônia felina atendida pelo projeto, que tinha em torno de 50 animais.

Segundo a ONG, Leer era carinhoso, enquanto os outros animais da colônia eram ariscos. Durante a captura, as voluntárias também notaram que ele tinha dificuldade para enxergar, aparentemente em razão do estrabismo .

No dia seguinte, o gato foi levado a um veterinário. Conforme o projeto, ele foi diagnosticado com calicivirose , uma infecção viral altamente contagiosa em gatos que afeta o sistema respiratório e causa feridas na boca, gengivas e língua e que exige que o gato não tenha contato com outros animais .

Leer já era castrado quando foi encontrado. Por isso, a ONG acredita que ele tenha vivido anteriormente com um tutor e sido abandonado na colônia.

O animal começou a receber tratamento no gatil mantido pela ONG. Segundo o projeto, ele apresentou melhora significativa. Depois de dois meses no gatil, Leer foi anunciado para adoção. O projeto considerava que a convivência com uma família poderia favorecer a recuperação, com atenção e cuidados individuais.

O projeto afirma que já havia recebido outros animais devolvidos, principalmente por dificuldades de adaptação. No caso de Leer, a justificativa foi divulgada nas redes sociais três dias depois do retorno dele ao gatil.

"A história dele me partiu o coração no meio. Me senti muito mau, triste e inconformado pela situação em que ele estava passando", afirmou Carlos Eduardo, que adotou o gato.

Carlos disse que decidiu se candidatar porque poderia oferecer atenção, espaço e tempo para cuidar do animal. Nos primeiros dias, segundo ele, o gato permaneceu apenas no quarto. Depois, passou a explorar os demais cômodos do apartamento.

Uma nova foto de Leer, dessa vez com uma expressão feliz, viralizou. Hoje, o gato procura carinho, permanece perto do tutor e até dorme na cama com ele.

"O fato de todas as noites quando eu deito ele pular na cama e em segundos vir pra próximo de mim pra dormir junto ajuda a perceber que ele se sente acolhido'", afirmou Carlos.

articles.title: Trisal com rainha de rodeio, irmã gêmea e agricultor está há 6 anos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Relacionamento repercutiu após Lara Alves Rueda contar em uma entrevista sobre o trisal. Maycon Rueda tem um filho de 5 anos com a Lara e um de 11 anos com a Laila.
articles.summary: Relacionamento repercutiu após Lara Alves Rueda contar em uma entrevista sobre o trisal. Maycon Rueda tem um filho de 5 anos com a Lara e um de 11 anos com a Laila.
articles.body:
O relacionamento a três entre a rainha de rodeio Lara Alves Rueda, de 35 anos, a irmã gêmea dela, Laila, e o agricultor Maycon Rueda, de 43 anos, ganhou as redes sociais após uma entrevista de Lara sobre a dinâmica da união , em Montividiu , no sudoeste de Goiás. Ao g1 , Maycon contou que o trio está junto há seis anos e vive em harmonia e felicidade. Segundo o agricultor, ele tem um filho de 5 anos com Lara e um de 11 anos com Laila.

"Eu sei que para a maioria do pessoal é estranho e perguntam como dá certo, mas a gente dá certo demais da conta, a gente é muito feliz. Elas são muito unidas por serem gêmeas, então parece que o sentimento de uma é meio que o sentimento da outra", disse Maycon.

Maycon explicou que cada um dos três tem um filho de relacionamentos anteriores. O filho dele mora em Uberlândia (MG) e o filho de Laila mora em Turvelândia, no sudoeste de Goiás. “Só a filha da Lara que mora com a gente” , contou.

Em entrevista ao g1 , a rainha de rodeio explicou a origem do relacionamento. Após namorar Maycon Rueda por dois anos e romper a relação, a irmã, Laila, viveu um namoro de quatro anos com o agricultor antes de propor que formassem uma família a três.

Trisal formado por rainha de rodeio, irmã gêmea e agricultor tem filhos e está há 6 anos junto: 'A gente é muito feliz’ — Foto: Arquivo pessoal - Maycon Rueda/Jam Carlos

Os três dividem uma casa de dois andares em Montividiu e organizaram a convivência de forma dividida : Laila fica no piso superior, enquanto Lara ocupa a parte de baixo por preferência pessoal, próxima à cozinha.

"Hoje a gente mora junto na mesma casa, só que é de dois andares. Ela ficou com a parte de cima, eu fiquei com a parte de baixo, que eu gosto de cozinha”, disse.

Maycon explicou que alterna as noites entre os dois pavimentos da casa para estar individualmente com cada companheira, pontuando que as irmãs não mantêm relacionamento íntimo entre si, mas compartilham uma forte ligação fraternal e de cumplicidade .

Apesar da curiosidade inicial dos moradores de Montividiu, o trio sempre contou com a aceitação dos familiares.

O agricultor reforçou que as dúvidas sobre o cotidiano superam os julgamentos. "O que eu mais escuto é curiosidade sobre como tudo funciona. Nunca imaginei ficar famoso por isso . Claro que tem críticas, mas é algo normal diante de um relacionamento fora do padrão", pontuou.

articles.title: Quando é o quinto dia útil de setembro 2026? Veja data para pagamentos | G1
articles.standfirst: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de setembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.summary: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de setembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.body:
Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de setembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário. — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil

Para trabalhadores com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de setembro de 2026 será sábado, dia 5 . Para o cálculo do prazo de pagamento de salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil, enquanto domingos e feriados não entram na contagem.

A regra está prevista no artigo 459 da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), que determina que o salário deve ser pago, no máximo, até o quinto dia útil do mês seguinte ao trabalhado.

Quando é o quinto dia útil de setembro de 2026?

No cálculo do prazo para pagamento do salário, são considerados os dias de segunda-feira a sábado. Domingos e feriados ficam fora da contagem.

Primeiro dia útil: 1º de setembro (terça-feira);

Segundo dia útil: 2 de setembro (quarta-feira);

Terceiro dia útil: 3 de setembro (quinta-feira);

Quarto dia útil: 4 de setembro (sexta-feira);

Quinto dia útil: 5 de setembro (sábado).

Portanto, para quem trabalha com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de setembro de 2026 é 5 de setembro.

Como a data cai em um sábado, o empregador deve observar as regras aplicáveis ao pagamento do salário para garantir que o valor esteja disponível ao trabalhador dentro do prazo legal.

Sábado conta como dia útil para o pagamento do salário?

Sim. Para a contagem do prazo previsto na CLT para pagamento de salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil.

A contagem é interrompida aos domingos e feriados. Por isso, mesmo que o trabalhador não tenha expediente aos sábados, o dia entra no cálculo do quinto dia útil.

Essa regra é específica para o prazo de pagamento do salário e não significa que o sábado seja necessariamente um dia normal de trabalho para todos os empregados.

O que acontece se o salário não for pago até o quinto dia útil?

O artigo 459 da CLT estabelece o prazo máximo para o pagamento do salário. Se o empregador não cumprir a data-limite, o trabalhador pode buscar orientação para cobrar os valores atrasados.

Em caso de atraso, o empregado pode recorrer à Justiça do Trabalho para cobrar o pagamento devido, com os acréscimos aplicáveis. O sindicato da categoria também pode auxiliar na defesa dos direitos dos trabalhadores e adotar as medidas cabíveis.

Atrasos frequentes ou prolongados no pagamento podem ainda caracterizar descumprimento das obrigações do empregador. Dependendo das circunstâncias, a situação pode levar ao reconhecimento de rescisão indireta, quando o trabalhador encerra o contrato e pode ter direito às verbas de uma demissão sem justa causa.

O empregador também pode estar sujeito à fiscalização e às penalidades previstas na legislação trabalhista.

articles.title: Fundações de Cultura e Sopro Novo firmam parceria | G1
articles.standfirst: Objetivo é promover curso de Educação Musical visando a formação de multiplicadores de ensino.
articles.summary: Objetivo é promover curso de Educação Musical visando a formação de multiplicadores de ensino.
articles.body:
Objetivo é promover curso de Educação Musical visando a formação de multiplicadores de ensino — Foto: Divulgação

Representantes da Fundação Sopro Novo Yamaha estiveram na Sede Administrativa da Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura para apresentar um projeto de parceria que será firmado entre as duas instituições, visando a promoção de cursos de Educação Musical para a população e a formação de multiplicadores de ensino.

Naoki Kirimura, CEO da Sopro Novo, e Otávio Rossato, supervisor de Planejamento e Operação, explicaram para os representantes do Poder Público, a metodologia e as opções de curso que poderão ser ministrados em Rio das Ostras.

O primeiro curso será “Aprendendo a Ler Música”, que é voltado para pessoas que ainda não leem partituras e desejam iniciar sua formação musical, além de professores que buscam compreender como a Metodologia Sopro Novo trabalha a alfabetização musical em sala de aula.

Nesse curso, serão ofertadas 10 vagas para a Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura voltadas para os professores do Centro de Formação Artística de Música, Dança e Teatro. O curso utiliza a flauta doce como ferramenta pedagógica fundamental, auxiliando o estudante a desenvolver a leitura musical de forma prática, estruturada e acessível. No entanto, o foco central é o domínio da leitura de partituras, por meio desse instrumento, que serve como base para a continuidade dos estudos musicais e para a atuação segura dos educadores junto aos seus alunos.

Para a presidente da Fundação Rio das Ostras de Cultura, Rosemarie Teixeira, a parceria vai beneficiar e valorizar ainda mais a Cultura do Município. “Será um ganho para nossos professores e alunos da Onda, que irão ter mais uma opção de aprendizado. O fato do curso formar outras pessoas que também vão ensinar Educação Musical também é de grande valia”, destacou.

Otávio Rossato ressaltou os trabalhos desenvolvidos no Município, na área Cultural. “Fiquei impressionado com a articulação e com a vida cultural existente em Rio das Ostras. Vimos o trabalho desenvolvido pelo Centro de Formação Artística na Feira da Onda e conhecemos muitas unidades culturais existentes aqui na Cidade. É encantador ver como se respira cultura aqui”, declarou o supervisor da Sopro Novo.

CURSO APRENDENDO A LER MÚSICA – O foco central do curso é o domínio da leitura de partituras por meio da flauta doce, que serve como base para a continuidade dos estudos musicais e para a atuação segura dos educadores junto aos seus alunos.

Dentre os objetivos estão desenvolver a leitura musical por meio da prática com flauta doce, compreender os fundamentos da teoria musical aplicada, adquirir autonomia para tocar e ensinar músicas simples e conhecer a metodologia Sopro Novo de alfabetização musical.

SOPRO NOVO – A Fundação nasceu em 2005 como iniciativa da Yamaha Musical do Brasil para ampliar o acesso à Educação Musical. Em 2017, transformou-se na Fundação Sopro Novo Yamaha, fortalecendo sua missão pública e ampliando sua autonomia para promover projetos educativos, firmar parcerias estratégicas e contribuir para o fortalecimento da música na Educação Básica.

A missão é democratizar o acesso à Educação Musical de qualidade, capacitando educadores para que possam atuar como multiplicadores em suas comunidades. A Sopro Novo acredita no poder transformador da música e trabalha para ampliar seu alcance por uma metodologia inovadora e acessível.

O programa atende educadores das redes públicas municipais, estaduais e federais, além de educadores de instituições privadas, como escolas regulares, escolas de música, igrejas e organizações sociais. Ao capacitar esses profissionais, a Fundação potencializa o impacto da Educação Musical, garantindo que ela chegue a estudantes de todas as idades e realidades em todo o Brasil.

articles.title: US strikes Iran's Larak Island after weeks of calm; Tehran retaliates by hitting US bases in Jordan
articles.summary: US News: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Sunday, in their first confirmed military action against Iran.
articles.body: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Sunday, in their first confirmed military action against Iran in a month, breaking a weeks-long lull in fighting. Iran quickly vowed retaliation, with state television later showing what it said were ballistic missiles fired at US bases in Jordan.Jordanian forces said they intercepted eight missiles that entered the country’s airspace early Monday. Meanwhile Iran international also reported that explosions were heard at US bases on Qatar. These attacks have not been confirmed by US officials.The US Central Command alleged Iran's Revolutionary Guard forces had been preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz when they were targeted. Tim Hawkins, a Centcom spokesperson, said the US military had observed the preparations, reported AP. The US had completed clearing sea mines from international shipping routes in the strait the previous week.Iranian semiofficial media, quoted by AP reported the explosions near Larak Island, while the Revolutionary Guard acknowledged that several of its fighters and civilians had been killed or wounded.The head of the national security commission of the Iranian parliament Ebrahim Azizi condemened the attack saying on X (translated from Farsi), "Retesting our will only makes the cost of your humiliating defeats even heavier. Undoubtedly, no crime, at any level, goes unanswered; a response that is devastating, more painful, and instructive, which will complete the chain of your failures. Wait in fear and terror!"He then made another statement in English adding, "Test our will once more, and pay a heavier price. Retaliation is coming; JUST RUN!"The strike marked the first confirmed US attack on Iran since July 29, when Washington said it had launched a “heavy wave of strikes” against dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets, including coastal surveillance and defence sites. President Donald Trump later said on August 1 that he would hold off on further strikes following appeals from Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.The latest military action came days after the Trump administration said it would prioritise economic pressure over further strikes in an effort to force Tehran to end the war. The strategy involved threatening sanctions against countries and entities that continue doing business with Iran.Revolutionary Guard spokesperson Gen. Hossein Mohebi called Sunday’s attack a “fatal mistake” and warned that Washington would face military and economic consequences.The administration’s reliance on sanctions also comes as US officials weigh depleted munitions stockpiles after more than six months of conflict, raising concerns about the impact on American military readiness elsewhere.Trump has increasingly played down the prospect of a quick end to the war, saying last week that he was “not in a hurry” to bring Iran back to negotiations. He has continued to argue that Iran’s leadership and military capabilities have been severely weakened.Iranian officials, however, have maintained a defiant stance. Recent appointments to senior security positions have signalled Tehran’s intent to continue resisting pressure despite years of sanctions and internal repression.Trump has repeatedly said the US-Israel campaign has devastated Iran’s navy and air force. Tehran estimates that the conflict has caused about $270 billion in direct and indirect damage, while Israeli strikes in the opening weeks severely weakened Iran’s political leadership.Despite those losses, Iran retains significant leverage through the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial global energy route. Tehran has targeted vessels in and around the waterway, where commercial traffic has fallen sharply since the war began.The strait normally carries about 20% of the world’s oil, but relatively few tankers carrying crude and liquefied natural gas are now willing to risk the route. Iran still possesses enough drones and missiles to threaten vessels passing through the waterway.Oil prices rose after Sunday’s US strike, with US crude gaining 1.8% to $84.94 a barrel and Brent crude rising 1.9% to $89.79.Iran has also maintained that the US cannot use the Strait of Hormuz until Washington fulfils its obligations under a memorandum of understanding signed with Tehran in June, even after Iran and Oman agree on a management arrangement for the waterway.Trump has repeatedly said the strait is “open”, pointing to 24 vessels that crossed it last week. That remains far below the roughly 130 vessels that passed through each day before the war.A US Navy-overseen multinational coalition said commercial traffic remained at “reduced levels” on Sunday. Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Organization said an unidentified projectile struck a tanker north of Khasab, Oman, on Saturday. No casualties or environmental damage were reported, and there was no immediate claim of responsibility.The US military said it had redirected 83 commercial vessels and disabled three others as part of its blockade of Iranian ports.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Sonia Gandhi: What will Congress leader's memoir reveal about India's most powerful political family?
articles.summary: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir may finally answer questions about power, loss and the Gandhi family’s political legacy.
articles.body:
When Sonia Gandhi became president of India's main opposition Congress party in 1998, she was an unlikely and largely enigmatic political leader.

Italian-born and the widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, she had spent years avoiding the political spotlight before taking charge of a party that had dominated much of independent India's history.

In her early months, India Today magazine described Sonia as "quite an enigma to her partymen" - "inscrutable", shielded from the world by a security cordon and known for her "laconic one-liners in an alien accent".

Yet beneath the reticence, the magazine detected a politician already learning how to exercise power. She listened to competing arguments, gathered information and then made up her own mind. "Nobody is left out of the decision-making process and no voice is gagged. But it is her word that prevails," it reported.

Nearly three decades later, after a political journey that took her from reluctant outsider to the most powerful figure in Congress, India's oldest political party, Sonia Gandhi is offering her own account.

The 79-year-old's story is marked by extraordinary personal loss: she rushed her mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, to hospital after her bodyguards shot her, and brought her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, home after a suicide bomber killed him seven years later.

Her autobiography, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which will be published in November by Alfred A Knopf in the US and William Collins in the UK, is likely to be one of the most closely watched political books in India.

In a statement issued through Alfred A Knopf, Gandhi says she wants this memoir "to be a testament of my heart's journey through the tender joys and dark despair that have marked my life".

According to William Collins, the book opens in Cambridge in 1965, where 19-year-old Italian student Sonia Maino falls in love with Rajiv Gandhi, grandson of India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.

In this "revelatory" account, the publishers say, the famously reticent Sonia looks back with "warmth and candour" on a life shaped by love, exile, political power and devastating loss - from her childhood in small-town Italy to her unexpected journey into the heart of Indian politics.

The memoir has already become the subject of a publishing dispute in India.

Reports that Penguin Random House India had sought changes to parts of the manuscript were followed by allegations from Congress leaders that the publisher had come under political pressure to alter passages critical of the government. Penguin has disputed that account, saying it "remained keen and willing to publish the book" while the "relevant discussions" were going on.

Yet readers will be looking for more than the story of how a young, foreign woman married into India's most powerful political family.

They will want answers to some of modern Indian politics' biggest unresolved questions: what drew her into politics, and what happened behind the scenes when the Congress returned to power in 2004 after eight years out of office?

The biggest mystery may be why Sonia, despite having the backing of her party and allies, declined the prime ministership and chose Manmohan Singh, the architect of India's economic liberalisation, instead.

Did she fear that her foreign origins would permanently undermine her government?

"I think that is really the biggest unanswered question. She could easily have become prime minister - she had the full backing of her party and allies, and the president's office had a letter ready inviting her to form the government," says journalist and author Neerja Chowdhury.

In his memoirs, former Congress leader and foreign minister Natwar Singh wrote that Sonia's son Rahul Gandhi was "vehemently" opposed to his mother becoming prime minister, fearing she would meet the fate of his grandmother and father.

Matters reached a "climax", Singh wrote, when Rahul said he was prepared to take "any possible step" to stop her. Will Sonia's memoir shed new light on that extraordinary decision - or offer a very different account of what really happened behind the scenes?

Whatever the reason, her decision transformed Indian politics. But that decision is only one part of a larger mystery: why did Sonia Gandhi enter politics in the first place?

She had spent years resisting a political career. After the assassination of Rajiv Gandhi in 1991, she remained largely outside public life. But as the Congress declined through the 1990s, she joined the party in 1997 and became its president less than a year later.

At the time, she was widely dismissed by her rivals. In December 1998, India Today reported that, initially, leading opposition politicians called her little more than a "housewife" or an "Italian wonder" . Yet, within months, she had begun transforming her party. One Congress veteran admitted: "I never thought that the lady could spring such a surprise."

The magazine was already detecting a formidable political operator. It described her as having an "iron fist under the velvet glove", and observed that she knew how to "cut down Himalayan egos to the height of foothills".

Then there are the tragedies that made her political career possible.

Sonia witnessed the transformation of her family after Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984. Seven years later, she lost Rajiv to a suicide bomber. The deaths changed the course of Indian politics - and her own life.

What will she say about those years? About Rajiv's political career, which she had strongly resisted? About the security fears surrounding her children? And about the moment she decided that the Gandhi family's political inheritance could not simply be abandoned?

Will she discuss Bofors , the scandal that badly damaged Rajiv Gandhi's government and generated decades of controversy around the family's links to Italian businessman Ottavio Quattrocchi? Will she revisit the allegations and explain what she knew?

And what about the furore over her Italian origins?

For years, Sonia was criticised as a foreigner who could not legitimately lead India. In Delhi's social circles, she was sometimes derided as "the Italian au pair". A person of foreign origin becoming prime minister, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Sushma Swaraj declared in 2004, "would be an insult to the nation"- she vowed to resign , tonsure her head, wear white and live as an ascetic if Sonia took the job.

"As early as in 1999, even a group of Congress leaders had raised questions about her foreign origins. Did she ever think of leaving the country?" says journalist and author Rasheed Kidwai.

Political observers also wonder whether the book could shed light on the paradoxes of the Congress-led government between 2004 and 2014.

Under Sonia's leadership, Congress won two successive national elections and backed landmark measures including the right to information law and the rural employment guarantee programme.

Yet its second term was overwhelmed by corruption allegations, policy paralysis and a growing sense that the party had become captive to its own leadership.

Sonia's critics called her the government's "remote control" - they wondered how much power she wielded over Singh. Her defenders saw her as the political force holding together a notoriously difficult coalition.

Sonia ultimately handed the Congress leadership to her son in 2017. Many believe his failure to revive the party is central to the story of the Gandhi family's decline.

In her 1994 book called Rajiv, Sonia wrote that she had "fought like a tiger" to prevent Rajiv from entering politics. Yet she eventually passed that inheritance to Rahul.

Rahul's political journey has hardly been smooth: he was once dismissed as a reluctant politician and often lampooned by rivals as an absentee leader.

"How does Sonia see her son's very different political style and worldview? And how much does she endorse his politics? I hope the book answers these questions," says Kidwai.

Another question is why Sonia chose Rahul, rather than his more naturally charismatic sister Priyanka, to carry the family's political legacy - and why Priyanka, despite years of speculation about a political role, only formally entered electoral politics in 2019.

"Sonia's stock answer would be that it would be up to my children to decide whether to join politics," says Kidwai.

There is a larger question, too: what does Sonia Gandhi think of the India she helped shape?

She led Congress during a period when Indian politics moved from coalition governments and economic liberalisation towards the much more dominant politics of Narendra Modi's BJP and Hindu nationalism.

But perhaps the most revealing question is what Sonia's memoir will choose to say - and what it will leave unsaid. Neerja Chowdhury suspects the answer may lie in the book's title, Belonging.

"She has been conscious of being an inheritor of the legacy of the Nehru-Gandhi family - that legacy has to be kept alive," Chowdhury says. She expects the memoir to return to family, its history, but above all to Sonia's own sense of belonging to the dynasty and of assuming its political mantle as Congress president.

That legacy, of course, is now under sustained attack.

The ruling BJP has campaigned for a "Congress-mukt Bharat" (Congress-free India), while critics of the party increasingly frame its challenge as a fight against dynastic politics.

As the Congress has suffered repeated electoral setbacks and watched many of its leaders defect to rivals, the question has become not just whether the Gandhi family can revive the party, but whether it can hold it together.

It is a question that goes to the heart of what Sonia says she is trying to examine in her memoir.

"Much has been written about my family, but few narratives were able to reach into the truth of their motivations, their actions and even their very human failings. In many ways, this book is a homage to their humanness," Sonia was quoted as saying on the book.

Her memoir may therefore be less a political reckoning than a defence of belonging - an attempt to explain what the Nehru-Gandhi inheritance has meant to her, and why she believes it still matters.

articles.title: This actor was told he had Alzheimer's, now he's performing a one-man show
articles.summary: Peter Marinker is taking on one of Samuel Beckett's most famous plays alone on a London stage.
articles.body:
For four days running, Peter Marinker had arrived at rehearsals that were not even taking place. Dementia had muddled the dates in his mind.

Yet he is now preparing to do something most actors would find daunting even with perfect recall: performing a much-loved Samuel Beckett play alone on a London stage.

Marinker, 85, is best known for his voice work: from radio plays and video games to big-budget films like Labyrinth and Paddington in Peru.

On camera he was the adviser to the US president in Love Actually and one of the airline passengers in the drama United 93.

In 2023 he was playing Gandalf in a stage version of Lord of the Rings when he felt himself "switching off" and an understudy had to take over for the rest of the run.

MRI scans and other health checks followed. Then two years ago, he was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease.

"I just had to accept it," he says. "It explained why I kept losing things and I started laughing at myself, at all the other silly things I do again and again."

At that point, some actors may have stepped back from the pressure of performing in front of a live audience.

But "out of the blue" a call came in from someone Marinker had worked with closely in the past - Dave Wybrow, the director of the Cockpit Theatre in London.

The idea was to put on Krapp's Last Tape, an intense one-man play in which an ageing writer listens back to recordings of his younger self, remembering a lifetime of regrets and missed opportunities.

"It's a dynamite show and a dynamite piece of writing," says Wybrow, whose mother also lived with memory problems at the end of her life.

Rehearsals have been running since the end of June to give Marinker extra time to practise, and a whole team assembled to make the play happen.

A stage manager will stand next to the set throughout the performances, autocue screens will be dotted around the theatre, and Marinker will be wearing a tiny earpiece so he can be quickly prompted if he forgets his lines.

Wybrow is adamant this is not about "covering up" Marinker's illness, but showing that collaborative, creative work is still more than possible after a dementia diagnosis.

From day one, Marinker says he did not have any concerns.

"Dave asked would I like to do it, and I was just 'Yes. Oh yes, yes, yes, yes!'" he says.

"I'll still get nerves [on the first night] but I know how to deal with them – that's just the adrenalin."

This is not the first time Marinker has performed the play. He first took on the same role in 1983.

The production team unearthed reel-to-reel recordings of that performance more than 40 years ago, and they will be woven into the new production as his character listens back to echoes of his younger self.

One of the striking things about Alzheimer's is that memory loss can be selective rather than uniform.

Early in the disease, regions around the hippocampus, deep within the brain's temporal lobes, are among the first to be affected.

That area plays a key role in forming and retrieving what scientists call episodic memories: memories of specific events and experiences in a person's life.

That is why people with Alzheimer's may struggle to recall a family holiday, a conversation with a friend or somebody's name, for example.

But other memories linked to highly practised skills and routines can be more resilient.

"Something stored in long-term consolidated memory is often easier to access than new memories that have just been formed," says Tara Spires-Jones, professor of neurodegeneration at the University of Edinburgh and author of Fighting for Our Minds.

That helps explain why some people with Alzheimer's can still make a cup of tea, recall song lyrics, or even perform music or a well-rehearsed theatrical script after other memories may have begun to fade.

All the profits from the four-day theatre run are going to the Alzheimer's Society, an organisation which helped Peter after his diagnosis.

Research for the charity in 2025 suggested that 42% of people living with dementia felt ashamed about their symptoms.

One-in-five of those with memory problems said they had not seen a doctor about a diagnosis because they were worried about the reaction of friends and family.

Stigma is "still very much prevalent", says Taiyaba Zeria, who manages dementia support services for the Alzheimer's Society in London.

"What Peter is doing really highlights that a diagnosis is not the end, and a person living with dementia can still do so many things they enjoy and they are passionate about."

Marinker, meanwhile, describes the project as his "wonderful swan song".

"I'm in the early stage [of the disease], so I need to make the best of the early stage and prepare as best I can for the middle stage," he says with a wry laugh.

"I might just live through this [performance], or I might just drop!"

Peter Marinker is appearing in Krapp's Last Tape at the Cockpit Theatre in London from 2 to 5 September.

articles.title: 12 million years ago, tiny dog-like animals crossed Nebraska as volcanic ash buried hundreds of animals; scientists have now found their footprints
articles.summary: US News: At Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park in northern Nebraska, researchers have spent decades excavating a mass graveyard created when volcanic as.
articles.body: At Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park in northern Nebraska, researchers have spent decades excavating a mass graveyard created when volcanic ash swept across the Great Plains roughly 12 million years ago. The eruption occurred in what is now southwestern Idaho, about 1,000 miles from the Nebraska site, but fine ash traveled across the continent and settled over a shallow watering hole where hundreds of animals had gathered. The site is best known for its remarkably preserved rhinos, horses and camels, many of which were buried where they stood. Now researchers have identified something else moving through the ash before the animals disappeared beneath it: large footprints made by caniform predators, the group that includes the extinct bone-crushing dogs known as borophagines. The tracks provide the first direct evidence that large carnivores were present at Ashfall, even though no skeleton belonging to one has yet been found.How volcanic ash buried a Nebraska watering hole 12 million years agoAccording to the University of Nebraska–Lincoln's Office of Research and Innovation, Ashfall preserves what was once a shallow depression that served as a seasonal watering hole. Fossils of pond turtles, reed-like plant remains and microscopic organisms known as diatoms indicate that water was present when the ash arrived. The site was not a permanent lake or stream-fed pond, however, and the geological layers show no evidence of the kind of channeling expected from continuously flowing water. The ash originated from a major volcanic eruption in what is now southwestern Idaho and traveled roughly 1,000 miles before reaching Nebraska. As the fine particles accumulated, animals around the watering hole were exposed to increasingly thick layers of ash. Many eventually suffocated, leaving their skeletons remarkably intact beneath the deposits.Why researchers know large predators were walking through the ashThe newly identified tracks were discovered in the same deposits that preserve the animals killed by the ashfall. Researchers believe they were made by large caniform predators, a group that includes the extinct bone-crushing dogs known as borophagines. Evidence of these predators had already existed at Ashfall in less direct forms. Researchers have found tooth marks on the bones of animals that died at the site, as well as coprolites containing fragments of bone. Those clues indicated that dog-like carnivores visited the site and fed on animals trapped by the disaster. The footprints add an important piece of evidence because they show the predators themselves moving across the landscape. Yet their skeletons remain missing. Unlike the rhinos, horses and camels that died at the watering hole, the predators apparently did not remain there long enough to become part of the mass burial.What the footprints reveal about the animals that survived the ashfallThe tracks suggest that large carnivores were moving through Ashfall while the catastrophe was unfolding. They may have been attracted by the concentration of vulnerable animals around the watering hole, creating an unusual opportunity for scavengers and predators. That interpretation fits the other evidence preserved at the site. Some herbivore bones carry tooth marks associated with bone-crushing dogs, while coprolites preserve the remains of bones that had passed through the digestive systems of dog-like carnivores. The footprints now provide physical evidence that animals from this group were actually present on the ground. Researchers are careful, however, about assigning the tracks to a particular species. Footprints can reveal an animal's size and movement but do not always provide enough information to identify the exact species responsible.How Ashfall became one of Nebraska's most unusual fossil sitesPalaeontologist Mike Voorhies discovered the first fossil at Ashfall in 1971, when he found the jaw of a young rhinoceros while studying the area's geology. Further investigations eventually revealed an extraordinary concentration of fossilised animals preserved in volcanic ash. A National Geographic-sponsored excavation followed in the late 1970s, helping bring the site to wider public attention. Ashfall officially became a Nebraska State Historical Park in 1991 through a partnership involving the University of Nebraska State Museum and the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission. One of the site's most unusual features is that many fossils are studied and displayed where they were originally found rather than being removed entirely from the deposits. Visitors can therefore see the animals in the same positions in which researchers uncovered them.Why researchers still have years of excavation aheadAshfall has been studied for decades, but large sections of the deposit remain unexplored. Researchers continue excavating during the summer, working carefully through the volcanic ash with small tools to expose additional bones, tracks and other traces of the ecosystem. The newly identified predator footprints are particularly valuable because they preserve something bones cannot: movement. A skeleton can reveal what an animal looked like, but tracks can show that it was walking through the site while the disaster was taking place. And the absence of predator skeletons does not mean the animals were absent. At Ashfall, the combination of footprints, tooth marks and fossilised droppings creates a picture of large carnivores entering a landscape filled with trapped prey, feeding among the dying animals and then disappearing before the ash finally sealed the scene. Twelve million years later, their footprints remain as some of the only direct evidence that they were ever there.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dark energy, exoplanets and black holes: What Nasa’s new Roman telescope will explore
articles.summary: US News: Nasa has launched its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on a mission to investigate dark matter and dark energy, study black holes and search for plan.
articles.body: Nasa has launched its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on a mission to investigate dark matter and dark energy, study black holes and search for planets beyond our solar system. The agency expects Roman's surveys to uncover roughly 100,000 new exoplanets.The telescope lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Sunday morning local time aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. The rocket released Roman 31 minutes into the flight, sending the observatory on a three-month journey to its final orbit around the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point, or L2, about one million miles from Earth.Roman's Wide Field Instrument will allow scientists to examine far more of the sky in a single observation. Nasa says its field of view will be at least 100 times larger than Hubble's. Its distant location will also help Roman's infrared instruments. Astronomer Jenifer Millard told the British Broadcasting Corporation this is to make sure infrared light from the Moon and Earth does not interfere with the cameras."Roman is going to change the way we look at the Universe," said Nicky Fox, a Nasa administrator.Roman could discover up to 100,000 exoplanetsOne of Roman's main scientific goals is to search for exoplanets, the name given to planets beyond our solar system. Fox said Roman "is going to discover tens of thousands, maybe even 100,000 new exoplanets" - referring to planets located outside of our solar system.It is expected to identify thousands of worlds in the Milky Way while its wider surveys reach much farther into space. "Why do we care so much about exoplanets? Because one of our main goals at Nasa is answering the question, 'Are we alone in the universe'?" she added. "One of our main goals at Nasa is answering the question: are we alone in the Universe?" Fox said at a Sunday morning news conference.The search will also contribute to scientists' broader efforts to understand whether worlds beyond our solar system could be habitable. "With Roman, we are going to make this giant leap forward... that is going to allow us to look at these distant, distant worlds and start to really resolve the atmosphere around them to let us know: could they be habitable?"Roman's destination is more than four times as distant from Earth as the Moon. Astronomer Jenifer Millard said the telescope will be four times further from Earth than the Moon is, where a lot of infrared space cameras - made to pick up what she describes as "heat light"- operate.Webb, which was launched in 2021, operates at a similar distance from Earth around the Sun-Earth L2 point. Roman, however, is designed to cover a much broader area of sky in a single observation. Hubble has been in space since 1990 and circles Earth at an altitude of roughly 300 miles.Roman will probe dark matter and dark energyRoman will also examine dark matter and dark energy, two phenomena that together are thought to account for about 95% of the Universe.Dark matter cannot be observed directly, but its presence can be inferred from its gravitational effects. Dark energy is the term scientists use for the still-unexplained phenomenon associated with the accelerating expansion of the Universe.Nasa says its "crisp, sweeping surveys will help scientists investigate dark energy and dark matter, discover and characterise exoplanets, map billions of galaxies, study black holes, and explore objects from our own solar system to the edge of the observable Universe."By observing galaxies across enormous distances, Roman could also give scientists a picture of how the Universe has changed over cosmic time. Millard said, through the work of telescopes like Roman, scientists are hoping to create "enormous cosmic maps" of the Universe at various stages."They'll be almost like an onion, so you can peel back layer upon layer... and see how the distribution of galaxies changes through cosmic time," she said. "What we want to do is use this distribution to try and figure out dark matter and dark energy because we know they exist, we see their effects, but what they are is a real mystery."Scientists hail successful launchThe launch later brought reactions from the scientists and officials involved in the mission.Jackie Townsend, a project manager on Nasa's Roman telescope, described it as "glorious" at a news conference afterwards. "The ride was magnificent. It put us right where we wanted to be."US President Donald Trump joined the space agency's news conference by phone to congratulate the scientists involved in Roman. "You're the hottest in space, and we have the hottest country anywhere in the world. So, let's keep it all going. You're a big part of it," he said.Telescope honours Nasa pioneer Nancy Grace RomanThe observatory is named after physicist Nancy Grace Roman. She became Nasa's first chief astronomer in the 1960s and was also the agency's first female executive.Roman spent years helping build support for the telescope that eventually became Hubble, including working to secure congressional approval and funding. She later identified dark energy as Hubble's most interesting discovery: the same mystery the observatory carrying her name will now help scientists investigate.Nasa plans five years of primary scientific operations for Roman and hopes the observatory can remain in service for a decade.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Travellers to Canada or those transiting through, here's the authorisation you may need
articles.summary: Tech News News: Canada's immigration authority has reiterated the entry requirements for foreign travellers heading to or passing through the country, according to th.
articles.body: Canada's immigration authority has reiterated the entry requirements for foreign travellers heading to or passing through the country, according to the latest guidance published on the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) website and shared by the department on social media. The authority said that depending on the nationality and the travel purpose, visitors may require an Electric Travel Authorisation (eTA) or a visa before boarding their flight. for the uninitiated eTA is a digital entry requirement linked to a traveller’s passport and is mandatory for visa-exempt foreign nationals flying to or transiting through Canada.Who needs an eTAFor citizens of eTA-eligible countries flying to Canada, an eTA and a valid passport are required to board a flight — a separate visitor visa is not needed in this case.The rules shift for travellers arriving by land or sea. In most cases, citizens of eTA-eligible countries arriving by car, bus, train, or boat, including cruise ships, do not need an eTA at all, though a valid passport is still required. One notable exception applies to travellers arriving by sea from Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon: those travellers do need an eTA to board, except when arriving by cruise ship.Certain visa-required travellers can also use an eTACitizens of select visa-required countries may also be eligible to apply for an eTA instead of a full visitor visa, but only if they are travelling to Canada by air. If those same travellers arrive by car, bus, train, or boat — including cruise ships — they still need a full visitor visa rather than an eTA.How to applyThe eTA application is completed online and usually approved within minutes, though some requests may take several days if additional documents are required. Travellers should apply before booking their flight to avoid delays. The eTA costs CAD $7 and is valid for up to five years or until the passport expires.Canadian citizens and permanent residentsCanadian citizens who also hold dual citizenship must travel using a valid Canadian passport. Canadian permanent residents do not need either an eTA or a visitor visa, but must travel with a valid permanent resident card or a permanent resident travel document. IRCC specifically flagged that permanent resident status does not expire — meaning former Canadian residents, even those who lived in the country long ago, may still hold valid PR status and should confirm their status before travelling to avoid complications.Travellers who need a full visaTravellers from visa-required countries, stateless individuals, and those holding a foreign passport for stateless persons must apply for a visitor visa rather than an eTA, regardless of how they plan to travel to Canada.US citizens and green card holdersAmerican citizens are exempt from the eTA requirement entirely and instead must carry the appropriate identification, such as a valid U.S. passport.Rules for U.S. lawful permanent residents ("green card" holders) have been in effect since April 26, 2022, requiring these travellers to present two categories of documents regardless of how they enter Canada: a valid passport from their country of citizenship (or an accepted equivalent travel document), and a valid green card or equivalent proof of their U.S. status. IRCC lists several acceptable forms of that status proof, including a valid Form I-551 permanent resident card, a foreign passport bearing a valid I-551 or ADIT stamp, or other specific combinations of expired cards paired with relevant USCIS notices, depending on a traveller's exact immigration paperwork situation.Basic entry requirements for everyoneBeyond authorization documents, IRCC outlined a broader set of baseline conditions all visitors must meet to enter Canada. Travellers must hold a valid travel document, such as a passport; hold a valid eTA or visitor visa; be in good health; have no criminal or immigration-related convictions; satisfy a border services officer that they have sufficient ties to their home country — such as employment, property, financial assets, or family — to ensure their return; convince the officer they intend to leave Canada at the end of their stay; and demonstrate sufficient funds to cover their visit, an amount that can vary depending on trip length and accommodation arrangements.Get the latest technology news and updates.
